# Ports

```as
/// Messages of type T from one lane to another, each a deep copy, bounded by
/// a byte capacity as a ring is. Posting never waits; receiving waits only
/// in an async call, a worker's or the main lane's, which settles on an
/// advance. A port is sendable, so the main lane hands ports to workers and
/// a request can carry the port its reply goes to; the sender may let go of
/// its own handle as soon as it posts.
/// ```as
/// export class Route {
///     from: f64 = 0;
///     to: f64 = 0;
/// }
///
/// // A service: it answers each request until it is stopped.
/// @worker export async function router(requests: Port<Route>, replies: Port<f64>): Promise<void> {
///     while (true) {
///         let request = await requests.receive();
///         if (request == null) {
///             return;
///         }
///         let route = request.value;
///         replies.post(route.to - route.from);
///     }
/// }
///
/// let requests = Port.create<Route>();
/// let replies = Port.create<f64>();
/// let worker = Worker.spawn(router, requests, replies);
/// requests.post(route);
///
/// // Later, in advance:
/// replies.drain((length: f64): void => {
///     this.length = length;
/// });
/// ```
@sendable
@sends
export class Port<T> extends LaneLocal {
    /// The ring the messages queue in.
    ring: Ring<T>;

    /// A port over ring, which it releases with itself.
    constructor(ring: Ring<T>);

    /// A port whose queued messages take at most capacityBytes, counted as a
    /// ring counts its records.
    static create<V>(capacityBytes: u32 = 4096): Port<V>;

    /// Queues a copy of value without waiting; false when the port is full
    /// right now, so a worker may await writable and post again. Throws for
    /// a message that, counted as a ring counts its records, is larger than
    /// the whole port, which never fits; send large data as a Blob, which
    /// crosses by id.
    post(value: T): bool;

    /// The oldest message, or null when none is queued; never waits.
    tryReceive(): Box<T>?;

    /// Hands each queued message to handler, oldest first, up to max of
    /// them, or by default those queued when it began, so a sender that
    /// keeps posting cannot hold it; answers how many it handed. The main
    /// lane's advance drains a port this way.
    drain(handler: (value: T) => void, max: i32 = -1): i32;

    /// As drain, handing messages until the given seconds have passed since
    /// it began, checked after each one, so it hands at least one when any
    /// is queued; it never waits. Only the main lane has a clock to budget
    /// a drain by.
    drainFor(handler: (value: T) => void, seconds: f64): i32;

    /// Settles with the oldest message once one is queued; with null once
    /// the given seconds pass without one, inside a worker being stopped, or
    /// when the port is gone. Each wait for a message starts the seconds
    /// over.
    async receive(seconds: f64 = Infinity): Promise<Box<T>?>;

    /// The oldest message, waiting on the main lane for one to be queued as
    /// Signal.waitWithin waits, so a worker can answer inside the call that
    /// asked; null once the given seconds or that wait's limits pass
    /// without one, or when the port is gone. Each wait for a message
    /// starts the seconds over. Only the main lane may block: a worker
    /// awaits receive.
    /// ```as
    /// requests.post(route);
    /// let reply = replies.receiveWithin(0.004);
    /// if (reply != null) {
    ///     this.length = reply.value;
    /// }
    /// ```
    receiveWithin(seconds: f64): Box<T>?;

    /// Settles true once a message was taken since the last post that did
    /// not fit, at once when the last post fit; false once the given seconds
    /// pass, inside a worker being stopped, or when the port is gone.
    /// ```as
    /// while (!port.post(block)) {
    ///     let room = await port.writable();
    ///     if (!room) {
    ///         return;
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    async writable(seconds: f64 = Infinity): Promise<bool>;

    /// Releases the port's ring as Shared.release does.
    release(): void;
}
